title: Fire Emblem's Best Seller Was Mostly Built by Another Studio
hook:
Intelligent Systems sent what its director called a minimum crew, and Koei Tecmo's Romance of the Three Kingdoms team built most of Fire Emblem: Three Houses. It became the best-selling game in the series. Which house did you pick first?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know the best selling Fire Emblem game was mostly built by the company behind Romance of the Three Kingdoms? Fire Emblem has been made by Intelligent Systems since the very first game in nineteen ninety. But when Nintendo planned the first Fire Emblem for the Switch, it wanted to shorten production time. Koei Tecmo was already making Fire Emblem Warriors for Nintendo. So Nintendo asked Koei Tecmo's Kou Shibusawa team, famous for Romance of the Three Kingdoms, to help build Three Houses. Intelligent Systems sent over what director Toshiyuki Kusakihara called a minimum crew. A handful of designers, a music composer, and an adviser for the programmers. Koei Tecmo was left in charge of basic game development, while the story, characters and core systems were still decided with Intelligent Systems. Aside from a few writers, most of the team came from Koei Tecmo. Kusakihara said the game simply would not have been possible without them. The Shibusawa team's experience with three warring kingdoms even shaped the setting of three balanced nations. After all of that teamwork, Three Houses finally launched on the Nintendo Switch in July of two thousand nineteen. It sold more than two and a half million copies in its first year, and became the best selling game in the series. Which house did you pick first? Follow for more gaming history.
